title: host-seam-can-be-sent-back-to-fixme
intention: host-seam v1, which can carry a WATCHME but has no BUILDME on its path, gains a FIXME repair edge so a host-seam WATCHME that cannot name its receiver can go back for fixing like every other watch-carrying class.
why: A WATCHME that cannot name its receiver goes back for fixing (Akien, answer to open-291189a9766a), with no class exception. 5f217a2d4bd6 gives the edge to bug, concept-piece and skill; host-seam v1 is the one watch-carrying class left without it, and its path has no BUILDME to re-enter, so the watch verb would refuse a host-seam fault and leave the ticket at WATCHME looking healthy.
traces_to: Akien's answer to open-291189a9766a; Law 4 (the rule in the class vocabulary); sibling of 5f217a2d4bd6 and 72d2f79daf0a.
how: Add repair_summons {"FIXME": "<step named by open-8bc1eaf1f568>"} to CairnCommons/node_classes/host-seam.json v1 with its why, through the artifact door; extend 5f217a2d4bd6's census proof to every WATCHME-carrying class and add a host-seam@v1 fixture tooth driving WATCHME -> FIXME -> the named step.
falsifier: Done when the watch verb handed holds=False for a host-seam@v1 fixture at WATCHME answers acted='fixme', the cursor stands at [FIXME], and FIXME exits to the step open-8bc1eaf1f568 names; a census over node_classes finds no WATCHME-carrying version lacking repair_summons. Wrong intent if Akien rules a host-seam watch fault goes elsewhere.
